what: The first mind slice and its two prerequisites: world/values.toml holds Schwartz's ten values (id and description) and the 0 to 4 importance words; every person file rates all ten (Rogue, Glitch and Mux with drafted, experiment-grade importances), validated at boot with file, path and rule; Engine.values serves each person's values on GET /api/values/<person> and a labelled Values section shows them with the importance as number and words; harness/src/jev.ts sends a JSON-object state and asks and parses score questions (score, legend, probabilities, confidence), pinned by a live body saved as a fixture; encountersOf forms one encounter per other recipient of each event, read by knowledge's people too; the bench splits into a player region (main: Act, Clock, Pending, Rooms, In transit, Items, History), the only part the harness reads, and an operator region (aside: Values, Knowledge, Encounters, Received), fully open; each score file records the page size its player read (#10); and the four goal sets re-run once against npc-encounters' 43 of 44.
why: Design B judges each encounter per value and weights the answers by the NPC's importance in code; that needs values on NPCs, a Jev client that asks in docs/jev.md's shapes, and encounters with everyone an NPC experienced in an event. The first run held 37 of 44 against 43 with the page doubled, so operator panels move out of the player's read by structure (#10). Design: docs/work/npc-values/shape/design.md.
stakes: The world's values are exactly the entries of world/values.toml, in its order, each an id and a description; no value id or description is written in code.
The importance words for 0 to 4 are authored in world/values.toml and are the only source of the words the bench shows.

Every person file rates every catalogue value with an integer from 0 to 4 and names no other value; a world that breaks this, or whose catalogue is missing, malformed or repeats an id, does not boot, and the refusal names the file, the path inside it and the rule.
Rogue, Glitch and Mux carry the drafted importances this design lists, each file marked as a draft.
Values are read from the loaded definitions on request and are never written to the state table or carried in the snapshot.

The page has one player region, the main landmark, holding Act, Clock, Pending, Rooms, In transit, Items and History, and one operator region, an aside holding Values, Knowledge, Encounters and Received fully open; the harness reads text and controls from the main landmark alone, so no operator panel's text reaches Jev's state, the target prompt or the vocabulary, and a page without exactly one main is a page stop.
Every score file records the mean and maximum page characters its runs' player read and the loop count they cover.

The bench serves each person's values on one route and shows them in a Values section in the operator region, each line labelled with the value's id, its importance as a number and in words, and its description, adding no control.

A person's encounters from an event it received are exactly one per other person who received that event, with role direct when it is the event's actor or a target and witnessed otherwise, read with no payload field and no subkind case.
Who a copy is with is computed only in encountersOf, and knowledge's people read it.

The Jev client sends a JSON-object state as an object and a string state as a string, and parses score answers (score, legend, probabilities, confidence) beside noul and choice, refusing as parse any answer missing a field or with level keys other than the question's levels as the live body keys them.
The harness imports nothing from the engine.
The score parser is tested against a raw body from one live call, saved as a fixture.
No per-encounter judgment, standing, edge, belief or summary is built.

The live probe and the first run of the four sets spent under the first $0.10; one re-run of the four sets after the page split spends at most a further $0.10, uses the default model and overwrites no committed score file.

criteria.then: it is wrong if the catalogue differs from the authored file or is held anywhere but definitions: defs.values is exactly ten entries, in world/values.toml's order, whose ids and descriptions equal, entry for entry, the values in corpus/experiments/value-weighting-3/catalogue.json; defs.importanceWords is the five phrases of catalogue.json's importance_scale for 0 to 4 in order; and no file under src/ contains any of the ten value ids or the five phrases as a literal (grep over src/)
criteria.atBase: loadWorld returns no values or importanceWords and world/values.toml does not exist, so the equality fails

mutations.change: hard-code the ten ids in definitions.ts instead of reading them from the file
read the importance words from a constant in code

criteria.given: a fresh temporary copy of world/ per case, each with one break
criteria.when: tests/values.test.ts calls boot() on each copy: values.toml removed; world.toml removed; a values.toml whose second entry repeats the first's id; a values.toml with importance key 4 removed; mux.toml's [values] missing benevolence; mux.toml's [values] naming greed = 2; mux.toml's power = 5; mux.toml's power = 2.5
criteria.then: it is wrong if any boots, creates a database, or names the wrong place: each returns ok false with refusal file, path and rule, respectively: values.toml, "", missing-file; world.toml, "", missing-file; values.toml, values.1.id, unique-value-id; values.toml, importance.4, zod's code; people/mux.toml, values.benevolence, value-rated; people/mux.toml, values.greed, value-names-catalogue; people/mux.toml, values.power, zod's code for too big; people/mux.toml, values.power, zod's code for a non-integer; and no database file exists at the dbPath after any of them
criteria.atBase: base has no values.toml check, its personSchema refuses any [values] table and a missing file reads as toml-syntax, so the expected files, paths and rules differ

mutations.change: read an unrated catalogue value as importance 0 instead of refusing

criteria.given: world/people/rogue.toml, glitch.toml and mux.toml as committed
criteria.when: tests/values.test.ts loads world/ and reads each file's text
criteria.then: it is wrong if a draft is missing, unmarked or altered: in catalogue order (self_direction, stimulation, hedonism, achievement, power, security, conformity, tradition, benevolence, universalism) Rogue's importances are 3, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 1, 0, 1, 0, Glitch's 2, 1, 1, 1, 0, 4, 3, 0, 1, 1 and Mux's 1, 0, 1, 3, 2, 2, 2, 1, 3, 1, and each file's text holds the comment line '# Draft importances (experiment-grade, drafted by the assistant, rudy 2026-11-10); derived from this world's ties.' directly above its [values] table
criteria.atBase: no person file has a [values] table, so every importance read is missing

criteria.given: world/ booted fresh, the engine and the bench's routes over it
criteria.when: tests/values.test.ts calls Engine.values for each person, acts rogue whisper glitch and steps once, calls it again, and reads readState(); tests/server.test.ts GETs /api/values/rogue, /api/values/nobody and /api/values/%E0%A4%A
criteria.then: it is wrong if values are not read from definitions or the route differs: Engine.values("rogue") is { person: "rogue", name: "Rogue", values } with ten entries in catalogue order, each { id, description, importance, words } where words is the importance's phrase (power: 4, "central to who this person is"); the result is equal before and after the act and step; no state row has part values; Engine.values("data-shard") throws; the route answers 200 with a body equal to Engine.values("rogue"), 404 naming nobody, and 400 for the malformed encoding
criteria.atBase: Engine has no values() and /api/values/ answers 404 for every person

mutations.change: store values as a person part written to the state table
show the importance number without its words

criteria.given: the bench served over world/ booted fresh
criteria.when: tests/page.test.ts reads the page's operator region, the aside landmark labelled Operator, fresh and again after rogue whisper glitch
criteria.then: it is wrong if the Values section is missing, unlabelled or closed: the aside's first h2 is 'Values'; under it each person has a level-3 heading 'What <name> values' with no parentheses, then ten list items, visible without any click, in catalogue order each reading '<id>: importance <n>, <words>, <description>' (Rogue's power line reads 'power: importance 4, central to who this person is, status and prestige, control or dominance over people and resources'); the section adds no control
criteria.atBase: base's page has no aside and no Values heading, so the section lookup finds nothing

criteria.given: world/ booted fresh, driven only through Engine.act and Engine.step, each case from its own fresh boot
criteria.when: tests/encounters.test.ts performs: mux departs west and the clock brings the arrive; then, from that state, glitch say; and separately rogue whisper glitch; and on a fresh boot glitch departs east with mux in the back room; and a refused action (mux offer stimpak to rogue), an invalid one (verb fly) and a tick-only step
criteria.then: it is wrong if an encounter is missing, extra, or of the wrong role: the depart gives mux none; the arrive gives mux one direct encounter with glitch and one with rogue, kind physical.arrive, and rogue and glitch each one witnessed with mux; glitch's say gives glitch one direct with mux and one with rogue, and mux and rogue each one witnessed with glitch and one witnessed with each other; rogue's whisper gives rogue one direct with glitch and one with mux, glitch one direct with mux and one with rogue, and mux one witnessed with glitch and one with rogue; glitch's depart east gives glitch one direct with rogue and rogue one witnessed with glitch, and mux, holding no copy, none from it; within a copy the others come sorted by id, each with that event's subkind, tick and id; the refused, invalid and tick-only steps leave every person's encounters unchanged
criteria.atBase: base's rule takes only actor and targets, so the say and the arrive give the actor no encounter and bystanders none with each other

mutations.change: read an arrive's payload present instead of the event's recipients
set role direct for every holder whose encounter is with the actor

criteria.when: tests/encounters.test.ts walks mux to the bar, then rogue whisper glitch, rogue say-to mux, mux say-to glitch, and reads each person's knowledge
criteria.then: it is wrong if knowledge's people keep the old rule: mux's people are the authored glitch then rogue as of the arrive (tick, source the arrive's id, subkind physical.arrive); glitch's are the authored rogue then mux as of the arrive; rogue's the authored glitch then mux as of the arrive
criteria.atBase: base takes mux's first encounter with rogue from the whisper, so mux's second person has the whisper as source

criteria.given: a local stand-in for the decisions endpoint that keeps each request body, passed as ClientOptions.endpoint
criteria.when: harness/test/jev.test.ts calls decide with the state { event: { text: "Rogue lets Glitch stay." } } and one noul question, then with the string state "Rogue lets Glitch stay."
criteria.then: it is wrong if the state is not sent as given: the first request body's state is the object, deep-equal to what was passed, not a string; the second's is the string; both carry model typesafe/jev-1.13 and the questions as given
criteria.atBase: decide's state parameter is typed string, so passing an object fails the harness typecheck that tests/harness-boundary.test.ts H1 runs over harness/test

criteria.given: harness/test/fixtures/jev-score-body.json, the live body V12 saved, served by a local stand-in endpoint
criteria.when: harness/test/jev.test.ts calls decide with the probe's three questions (a noul, a choice and a three-level score), then with the fixture altered once per case: legend removed; a probabilities key outside the score's levels; score a string; confidence removed
criteria.then: it is wrong if the score answer is not returned as the wire gave it or a malformed one passes: the noul answer is the fixture's noul, the choice answer its choice, confidence and probabilities, and the score answer exactly { score, confidence, legend, probabilities } with the fixture's values, legend keyed by the levels as the fixture keys them; each altered body gives ok false with refusal kind parse naming the score question
criteria.atBase: base's parser reads a score answer as a choice, finds no string choice and refuses with parse, so the unaltered fixture fails

mutations.change: accept a score answer with no legend
derive and return a most-probable level in place of probabilities

criteria.given: a local stand-in endpoint answering fixed noul and choice bodies
criteria.when: harness/test/jev.test.ts calls decide with a noul and a choice question and a string state, and with a body missing the choice's probabilities
criteria.then: it is wrong if noul or choice parsing changed: the noul answer is { noul } and the choice { choice, confidence, probabilities } as served, costUsd is usage.cost or null, and the body missing probabilities gives a parse refusal naming the choice question
criteria.atBase: base parses noul and choice answers this way already

criteria.given: harness/ copied alone into a fresh directory, as tests/harness-boundary.test.ts H1 does
criteria.then: it is wrong if the harness reaches the engine: the typecheck passes, the tests pass, and every file its program lists lies under the copy or the linked node_modules
criteria.atBase: base's harness imports nothing outside itself

criteria.given: The approved spend (strata-d3 for rudy, 2026-11-10): at most $0.10 USD for this probe call and the first run of the four sets together, already spent at $0.069170. The built jev.ts, before its score key rule is final.
criteria.when: the builder runs bun corpus/experiments/npc-values/probe.ts once, which sends through decide() the JSON state { event: { text } } with one noul, one choice and one three-level score question, each instruction naming event.text
criteria.then: it is wrong if the fixture is not a real, scrubbed body: harness/test/fixtures/jev-score-body.json exists, its top-level keys are exactly answers, model and usage, its answers hold the three question names, and corpus/experiments/npc-values/probe.txt records the run's date, its costUsd and the parsed answers; harness/test/jev.test.ts asserts the fixture's keys
criteria.atBase: no fixture exists at base, so reading it fails

criteria.given: The approved spend (strata-d3 for rudy, 2026-11-10): the probe and the first run of the four sets spent $0.069170 of a first $0.10; one re-run of the four sets after V14 and V15 are built may spend up to a further $0.10 USD, default model and default Jev, with no further approval needed within it; the builder stops and reports if it would pass it. mux-speaks-up lost to a bare `say` for `speech.say` is accepted as a model naming loss (strata-d3, 2026-11-10). The job's built code, V14 and V15 included, passing the gate, and corpus/goals/knowledge.json, blind-1.json, blind-2.json and blind-2-spent.json copied unchanged to corpus/experiments/npc-values/.
criteria.when: bun run score --goals corpus/experiments/npc-values/<set>.json --tick-minutes 10 runs once for each of the four with the default model, after the player region is built, replacing the first run's score files
criteria.then: it is wrong if a committed score file changes, a loss goes unexplained, or the page result is missing: each copy's sha256 equals its corpus/goals original's; git diff -- corpus/goals is empty; four score files exist under corpus/experiments/npc-values/, each with its page field; docs/work/npc-values/real-runs.md gives held and costUsd per set beside npc-encounters' run of the same sets (43 of 44 in all, the bar), each set's page meanChars and maxChars beside npc-encounters' computed the same way from its loops.jsonl, the first run's totals (37 of 44, page doubled) as the record that led here, the total spend, and every goal not held with its cause from its loops.jsonl and run.json; any loss a code path decided (a vocabulary or checked() refusal of a name the page served) is fixed before merge; the run directories are copied to the main checkout's corpus/runs before the job's result is handed back
criteria.atBase: no copies, score files or real-runs.md exist under the npc-values paths, so the checks fail

criteria.given: the bench served over world/ booted fresh and driven, read by harness/src/page.ts readPage
criteria.when: tests/page.test.ts reads the page fresh and after mux walks to the bar, rogue whisper glitch and rogue offer data-shard to glitch, renders the read into renderState and the target prompt, and separately serves a page with no main element and one with two
criteria.then: it is wrong if any operator panel's text reaches the player: the read's text holds none of the headings Values, Knowledge, Encounters or Received, no 'What <name> values' or 'What has passed between' heading and no value line, and neither does renderState()'s nor the target prompt's text; main's h2 headings are exactly Act, Clock, Pending, Rooms, In transit, Items and History in that order; the read's controls are exactly the controls inside main, so the Received viewer select is not among them; vocabulary() gives exactly the world's people, items, rooms and exits; and the run over a page with no main, or with two, stops with kind page naming it, before any loop

mutations.change: read the body when no main is found
render the Knowledge section inside main
collect controls from the whole document

criteria.given: a goal set whose runs' loops.jsonl states are written by hand with known page texts after 'The page now:\n' (three loops of 10, 20 and 60 characters)
criteria.then: it is wrong if the page size is missing or miscounted: the score file's page is { loops: 3, meanChars: 30, maxChars: 60 }, and a set whose loops are none gives { loops: 0, meanChars: 0, maxChars: 0 }
criteria.atBase: base's score file has no page field

walks.when: after merge, on main: bun run start --tick-minutes 10, open http://127.0.0.1:4800, act mux depart west, press Step
walks.then: the page shows the World region with Act, Clock, Pending, Rooms, In transit, Items and History, and beside or below it the Operator region, fully open, with Values ('What Rogue values', 'What Glitch values', 'What Mux values', ten lines each such as 'power: importance 4, central to who this person is, ...' under Rogue), Knowledge, Encounters (under 'What has passed between Mux and others', 'with glitch' and 'with rogue', each 'role direct (actor or target), kind physical.arrive, tick 1, event <id>') and Received; every line reads as labelled
walks.operatorOnly: Whether the two regions and the Values and Encounters sections read clearly to a person at a glance is a human reading of the rendered page; the page tests prove the text, the regions and the vocabulary, but no command can judge legibility.

outOfScope.summary: An actor now holds an encounter with every other person who received its act, so a depart, an arrive or a say to the room makes encounters for the actor with everyone who saw it.

frequency.records: corpus/runs/**/received.jsonl: actor's encounters with a recipient outside its act's targets, of all corrected-rule encounters

outOfScope.summary: Two bystanders of the same event, such as a whisper between two others, now hold a witnessed encounter with each other.

frequency.records: corpus/runs/**/received.jsonl: bystander-with-bystander encounters, of all corrected-rule encounters

outOfScope.summary: Knowledge's people change: an arriver lists the room's people as of its arrival, and a bystander lists other bystanders.

frequency.records: corpus/runs/**/received.jsonl: arrive events with another recipient besides the mover, of all arrive events

outOfScope.summary: The importances of Rogue, Glitch and Mux are the assistant's draft from three ties notes, not authored by rudy.

frequency.records: world/people/*.toml: people files with no [values] table, each drafted here, of all people files

outOfScope.summary: Every world, test worlds included, must author the full catalogue and every person's full table; there is no default.

frequency.records: world/ and tests/worlds/*: world directories with a people/ folder that must author the catalogue and full tables, of all such directories

outOfScope.summary: The client returns a score answer as the wire gives it, with no most-probable level; a caller buckets the score itself.

frequency.reason: No caller asks a score question yet (grep -rn '"score"' harness/src src outside jev.ts counts 0); the first, the per-encounter judgment, buckets its score itself per docs/jev.md rule 6.

outOfScope.summary: The player no longer reads the Knowledge, Encounters and Received panels, and the Received viewer select is no longer a candidate it can choose; the knows end state is still checked on its route.

frequency.records: world/people/*.toml: people files whose drafted importances rest on a ties note, of all people files
